Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> A Cruise autonomous vehicle and a San Francisco fire truck collided at the intersection of Turk and Polk streets on the evening of August 17, 2023. The fire truck was responding to an emergency in "Code 3" mode, with its lights and sirens active at the time of the crash. According to Cruise, its vehicle entered the intersection on a green light when it was struck. The single passenger in the Cruise robotaxi was transported to a hospital with injuries described as non-life-threatening. Following the incident, which was reported by news outlets on August 18, 2023, the California Department of Motor Vehicles requested that Cruise reduce its operational fleet in the city by half. <2> On August 10, 2023, the California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) voted 3-to-1 to approve resolutions allowing Waymo and Cruise to operate commercial, driverless robotaxi services 24/7 throughout San Francisco. This decision marked a significant expansion of their operations, which were previously restricted. The approval permits both companies to charge fares for driverless rides at any time of day. Waymo's authorization also includes offering full service into parts of neighboring San Mateo County (the peninsula). The decision was met with both support, citing benefits for safety and accessibility, and opposition from city agencies and some residents concerned about the technology's readiness and incidents of vehicles disrupting traffic and emergency responders. <3> In 2023, Waymo, the autonomous vehicle subsidiary of Alphabet Inc., undertook significant restructuring which included multiple rounds of layoffs and the discontinuation of its autonomous trucking program, Waymo Via. Throughout the year, Waymo conducted three rounds of job cuts. The first occurred in January as part of broader layoffs at its parent company, Alphabet, which let go of 12,000 employees. The second round in March saw 209 employees, primarily from engineering, laid off, representing 8% of its workforce at the time. A third, smaller round of layoffs was announced in October as part of an internal reorganization. On July 26, 2023, Waymo officially announced it was "pushing back the timeline" on its commercial and operational efforts in trucking to focus its investments and resources on its primary ride-hailing service, Waymo One. This move was seen as a shutdown of the Waymo Via trucking division, which had been operating since 2017. The decision followed rumors and was framed as a strategic choice to capitalize on the momentum in the robotaxi market. <4> On July 26, 2023, the U.S. House of Representatives' Subcommittee on Innovation, Data, and Commerce held a legislative hearing titled 'Self-Driving Vehicle Legislative Framework: Enhancing Safety, Improving Lives and Mobility, and Beating China.' The hearing, announced on July 24, 2023, examined a draft bill aimed at establishing a national framework for the regulation of autonomous vehicles (AVs). Key discussion points included the potential for AVs to enhance safety, improve mobility for individuals with disabilities, and the importance of the U.S. staying competitive with China in this technological domain. Lawmakers and witnesses discussed the need to expand exemptions for testing and deployment to foster innovation. The proposed legislation would grant the Secretary of Transportation authority to set national standards for automated driving systems and to prohibit vehicles that pose a security risk. Concerns were also raised by some Democrats, safety groups, and labor unions regarding potential liability loopholes and the impact on jobs. Witnesses at the hearing included representatives from the National Federation of the Blind, the Alliance for Automotive Innovation, the Consumer Technology Association, and Carnegie Mellon University. <5> On June 16, 2023, Aurora Innovation, Inc. announced the public release of the Aurora Multi-Sensor Dataset, a large-scale, open-source collection of autonomous driving data, in collaboration with the University of Toronto. The dataset was previously introduced as PIT30M at the International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS) in 2020. The dataset aims to help researchers develop more robust and reliable self-driving systems by providing rich data captured by a 64-beam Velodyne LiDAR sensor and seven high-resolution cameras. The data includes semantic segmentation, spans all four seasons with varied weather and traffic conditions, and was collected in Pittsburgh, PA, by Uber's Advanced Technologies Group (ATG), which Aurora acquired in 2021. Hosted on Amazon Simple Storage Service (S3), the dataset is available for non-commercial academic use. <6> Aurora Innovation, a self-driving technology company, announced the promotion of David Maday to Chief Financial Officer, effective June 14, 2023. The public announcement was made on June 15, 2023. Maday, who previously held the position of Senior Vice President of Business Development and Product Strategy, succeeded Richard Tame. Tame stepped down to pursue other opportunities and was slated to remain with the company until August 31, 2023, to ensure a smooth transition. Before his time at Aurora, Maday had a 20-year tenure at General Motors, where he was involved in transforming the company's Product Program Finance organization. <7> An analysis of data from the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) by The Washington Post revealed that Tesla's Autopilot was involved in 736 accidents in the United States from 2019 through 2023, a figure higher than previously reported. The data, which NHTSA began collecting systematically after a 2021 federal order, showed a significant increase in crashes and associated fatalities, with at least 17 fatal incidents and five serious injuries linked to Autopilot during this period. Of the 17 fatalities, 11 occurred after May 2022, coinciding with an expansion of Tesla's "Full Self-Driving" software. The increase in reported incidents followed a mandate requiring automakers to disclose crashes involving driver-assistance technology. In response to the findings, Tesla maintains that its Autopilot system, when used, results in a lower crash rate per million miles driven compared to vehicles without it, citing its own quarterly safety reports. However, the NHTSA data has led to ongoing investigations into the technology.

Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> S&P Global Mobility released an analysis on June 27, 2024, based on its 2024 consumer survey of nearly 8,000 people across eight countries, which found that while consumer trust in autonomous vehicles is gradually increasing, it remains cautiously optimistic. [2, 4] The survey highlighted a strong and consistent interest in Advanced Driver-Assistance Systems (ADAS), with blind-spot detection being a favorite feature for the fourth consecutive year. [4] In contrast, driver facial monitoring was the least desirable feature, a sentiment possibly linked to privacy concerns. [4] The analysis also revealed that while over half of global respondents are familiar with ADAS features like park assist and collision warning, they are generally less willing to pay extra for higher levels of automation, preferring feature bundles over individual options. [2, 6] Overall, consumers showed more trust in established German premium automakers to develop safe self-driving vehicles. [4] <2> On June 20, 2024, the California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) upheld a previous decision from March to permit Waymo, a subsidiary of Alphabet, to expand its driverless taxi services. [2, 3] This expansion allows Waymo to operate in the San Francisco Peninsula, including San Mateo County, and Los Angeles, moving beyond its initial San Francisco-based operations. [2, 4] The reaffirmation came despite protests and concerns from local officials and bodies, such as San Mateo County Supervisor David Canepa, who voiced worries about the technology's readiness and safety. [2, 3] The decision was made after a bill that would have granted local governments more control over autonomous vehicle regulations was withdrawn from the state legislature. [2] While Waymo can now proceed with the expansion, a specific timeline for the full commercial launch of paid services in the new areas has not been announced. [2] <3> Waymo announced an expansion of its autonomous ride-hailing service, Waymo One, in the Phoenix metropolitan area by an additional 90 square miles, bringing the total service area to 315 square miles. [5] The expansion, which commenced on June 5, 2024, extends further into North Phoenix, reaching areas like Desert Ridge, and includes more of Scottsdale's resorts and attractions such as TPC Scottsdale. [3, 5] This development makes Waymo's Phoenix service area the largest autonomous ride-hail territory in the United States. [5] In a separate first, the service now also operates on tribal land through a partnership with the Salt River Pima–Maricopa Indian Community, providing access to the Talking Stick Entertainment District. [5] <4> Tesla released its Q1 2024 Vehicle Safety Report, revealing that vehicles utilizing Autopilot were involved in one crash for every 7.63 million miles driven. This figure marks a significant improvement in safety performance. For comparison, drivers not using Autopilot recorded a crash for every 955,000 miles driven. The U.S. national average, according to the most recent data from NHTSA and FHWA from 2022, was approximately one crash every 670,000 miles. Tesla had paused the publication of this report after the fourth quarter of 2022 and has now released the data for the intervening quarters alongside the Q1 2024 results. Some critics point out that the data's usefulness is limited because it doesn't account for the different driving environments where Autopilot is most commonly used, such as highways, which typically have lower accident rates. <5> Volvo Autonomous Solutions (V.A.S.), in collaboration with Aurora Innovation, officially unveiled its first production-ready autonomous truck, the Volvo VNL Autonomous, on May 20, 2024. The launch event took place at the ACT Expo in Las Vegas. [4] This purpose-built vehicle, powered by the Aurora Driver, is designed for the hub-to-hub long-haul freight segment. The truck will be assembled at Volvo's New River Valley (NRV) plant located in Dublin, Virginia. <6> The U.S. National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) initiated an investigation into Waymo's 5th generation automated driving system following 22 reports of its robotaxis exhibiting unsafe driving behaviors. [4, 5, 10] These incidents included 17 collisions and other potential violations of traffic safety laws, such as crashing into stationary objects like gates and parked vehicles, driving in opposing traffic lanes, and entering construction zones. [5, 10] The investigation, opened on May 13, 2024, aimed to evaluate the performance of an estimated 444 Waymo vehicles in detecting and responding to traffic control devices and avoiding collisions with both stationary and moving objects. [4, 8] Waymo stated its commitment to cooperating with the investigation. [4] <7> The U.S. National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) opened a preliminary evaluation into Amazon's self-driving unit, Zoox, after two of its vehicles, both Toyota Highlanders equipped with the Zoox Automated Driving System (ADS), braked suddenly and were subsequently rear-ended by motorcyclists. [1, 2, 3, 4] The investigation, designated as PE24015, was officially opened on May 10, 2024, to evaluate the performance of the Zoox ADS, particularly its behavior in scenarios leading to rear-end collisions and its conduct near crosswalks and vulnerable road users. [7, 10] The two incidents, which resulted in minor injuries to the motorcyclists, occurred during daytime conditions while the ADS was engaged. [3, 8, 10] One crash took place in San Francisco, California, and the other in Spring Valley, Nevada. [3, 9] The probe covers an estimated 500 Zoox vehicles. [4, 7] <8> The U.S. National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) closed a multi-year engineering analysis (EA22-002) into Tesla's Autopilot system after identifying a "critical safety gap" between the system's capabilities and drivers' expectations. [1, 2] The investigation, which began in 2021, analyzed 956 crashes and found that foreseeable driver misuse played a role in at least 13 fatal crashes and numerous others involving serious injuries. [1, 2, 10] NHTSA concluded that the Autopilot's driver engagement system was inadequate for its permissive operational capabilities, leading to preventable accidents. [2, 6] The closure of the probe followed a December 2023 recall by Tesla of over 2 million vehicles to update the Autopilot software. [1, 3] However, concurrently with closing the investigation, NHTSA opened a new probe (Recall Query RQ24-009) to evaluate the adequacy and effectiveness of that recall. [5, 10] The agency cited concerns over crashes that have occurred since the software update and noted that some remedy features require an owner to opt-in and can be easily reversed by the driver. [1, 18]

[5, 7] This testing phase marks a significant step since the collaboration was first announced in December 2021 and introduces a new vehicle platform to Waymo's fleet, which has primarily consisted of retrofitted Jaguar I-PACEs and Chrysler Pacifica hybrids. On July 23, 2024, during its Q2 2024 earnings call, Alphabet CFO Ruth Porat announced a new investment commitment of up to $5 billion in Waymo to help it continue to build the world's leading autonomous driving company. This funding will be distributed over several years. Subsequently, on August 19, 2024, Waymo unveiled its sixth-generation Waymo Driver system. This new iteration features a more cost-effective sensor suite, reducing the number of cameras from 29 to 13 and offering enhanced resolution, range, and performance in various weather conditions. <8> S&P Global Mobility released an analysis on June 27, 2024, based on its 2024 consumer survey of nearly 8,000 people across eight countries, which found that while consumer trust in autonomous vehicles is gradually increasing, it remains cautiously optimistic. [2, 4] The survey highlighted a strong and consistent interest in Advanced Driver-Assistance Systems (ADAS), with blind-spot detection being a favorite feature for the fourth consecutive year. [4] In contrast, driver facial monitoring was the least desirable feature, a sentiment possibly linked to privacy concerns. [2, 3] The decision was made after a bill that would have granted local governments more control over autonomous vehicle regulations was withdrawn from the state legislature. [2] While Waymo can now proceed with the expansion, a specific timeline for the full commercial launch of paid services in the new areas has not been announced. [5] The expansion, which commenced on June 5, 2024, extends further into North Phoenix, reaching areas like Desert Ridge, and includes more of Scottsdale's resorts and attractions such as TPC Scottsdale. [3, 5] This development makes Waymo's Phoenix service area the largest autonomous ride-hail territory in the United States. [5] In a separate first, the service now also operates on tribal land through a partnership with the Salt River Pima–Maricopa Indian Community, providing access to the Talking Stick Entertainment District. While the company began commercial driverless operations in May 2025, the addition of nighttime routes more than doubles the potential utilization of the trucks.
